test_case.name: Resource Request Limits (Unschedulable Pod / Insufficient CPU & Memory)
test_case.scenario_description: Pod 'fraud-detection-model-9a8b7c6d5-p4l2k' (container 'inference-server', namespace 'risk-engine') is deployed with excessive resource requests (requests.cpu=16000m, requests.memory=64Gi) on a 6-node cluster of 8-vCPU / 32Gi worker nodes. The Kubernetes scheduler rejects all candidate nodes with FailedScheduling ('0/6 nodes are available: 4 Insufficient cpu, 6 Insufficient memory'), leaving the pod stuck in Pending.
test_case.injected_fault: Oversized pod resource requests (cpu: 16, memory: 64Gi) exceed maximum single-node allocatable capacity (8 vCPU, 32Gi).
test_case.ground_truth_rca: Pod 'fraud-detection-model-9a8b7c6d5-p4l2k' is stuck in Pending state because its container resource requests (16 CPU cores, 64Gi RAM) exceed the allocatable capacity of all 6 worker nodes ('0/6 nodes are available: 4 Insufficient cpu, 6 Insufficient memory').

suggested_remediation: Inspect cluster node capacities and allocatable resources: `kubectl describe nodes | grep -A 8 'Allocated resources'`.
Verify pod resource requests and limits (`spec.containers[*].resources`) to ensure they match workload needs and node sizing.
Lower excessive pod `resources.requests` to fit within worker node allocatable capacity, or scale out the node pool.
Review namespace ResourceQuota and LimitRange constraints: `kubectl describe quota,limitrange -n <namespace>`.
